notes: No past-tense verbs or adjectives whose subject is the player, another player or a {name} (they would state a gender): present tense, impersonal forms (zbudowano, opuszczono) or nouns (Najazd na twoją wioskę: {name}).
Placeholders stay in the nominative: after a colon or in apposition to a declined noun (budynek {building}); no case ending or case-governing preposition is attached to a placeholder.
Plurals use one, few, many and other (other for fractions), as Intl.PluralRules("pl") gives.

Generated names need generatedNames: noun-first. Second parts are nouns (Szczyt, Przełęcz, Dolina, Żuraw), first parts genitive nouns that fit every gender (Gromu, Mgieł, Żelaza, Ciszy): Przełęcz Gromu, Żuraw Ciszy.

Polish letters ą ć ę ł ń ó ś ź ż (beyond ó) are outside the bundled Latin-1 font subsets, so pl must be added to SYSTEM_FONT_LANGS and the html:is([lang=…]) rule at activation; tests/locales/latin-fonts.test.ts fails until then.
The Japanese statutory pages are translated into Polish (titles included), following the Vietnamese pattern.
Computer players' generated names (Kaito Mori) stay in Latin letters, as in every language.
